notes: SHIP v1.14.361 - RENAME the deploy banner raster to the name the owner's ruling used. icons/phantom-banner-deploy-1170.webp becomes icons/DEPLOY-phone@3x.webp, by owner ruling 2026-07-30 ('yes rename it to DEPLOY-phone@3x.webp'). This closes the filename deviation reported in .360: the release ruling named a file that existed nowhere, .360 referenced the real .357 asset instead and reported the mismatch, and the owner has now ruled the name rather than the file. THREE THINGS MOVE AND NOTHING ELSE: the file (git mv, so history follows it and the raster bytes are untouched - 43134 bytes before and after, still 1170x403), the in the DEPLOY .bnr row, and the PRECACHE_URLS entry. The art itself was NOT re-staged, re-encoded or re-cropped. WHY A VERSION BUMP FOR A RENAME: this changes a SERVED ASSET PATH and a precache key. A client on the old service worker has the old URL cached and would 404 the new one, so the CACHE_VERSION bump is what makes the swap safe - the new SW builds a fresh cache from the new list and the activate handler deletes the old. A rename without the bump is an offline-boot break, which is exactly the failure class the banner ships have been guarding. URL SAFETY OF '@': legal unencoded in a path segment - RFC 3986 defines pchar as unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ':' / '@' - so no percent-encoding is needed or wanted. The string and the PRECACHE_URLS string are byte-identical, which is what makes the Cache API match: both resolve against the same base to the same request URL. A mismatch there would present as the DEPLOY row falling back to the accent hatch offline while looking fine online. NAMING IS NOW MIXED, DELIBERATELY AND BY RULING: the other four banners keep phantom-banner-{scan,master,ops,handoff}-1170.webp. DEPLOY alone carries the new name, and it is the only asset in icons/ using either the @Nx suffix or SCREAMING-CASE. That is the owner's call, executed as given. If the intent was a new convention for the whole set rather than one file, the other four are a four-line sweep in a follow-up - not assumed here, because renaming four working assets on inference is exactly the kind of unasked-for change that breaks an offline install. BATCH POSITION - FLAGGED: this is the SEVENTH ship in batch .355-.361, one past the CALL-0 six-ship cap, and the batch was already due on two independent grounds (the cap itself, and HIGH-risk .359). Shipped anyway on direct owner instruction; precedent exists (.208 stacked one past the cap by owner decision 2026-07-08). The consolidated device pass is now overdue and nothing further should ship before it clears. GATES: three-stamp lockstep; inline JS compiles (4 of 4 blocks) plus sw.js; CSS braces balanced in all 12 style blocks; diff is two reference lines plus the stamps; the renamed file exists on disk at the new path and is precached under the identical string; zero references to the old filename remain in either live file; the .359 acceptance checks re-run green (5 banner rows, 9 wall cells); the .359 rows, OPS wall, handlers, registry and CSS are untouched. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) badge reads v1.14.361. (2) BUILD: the DEPLOY row still shows its photograph - if it shows the diagonal accent hatch, the rename broke the reference and the fallback is telling you so. (3) The other four rows are unchanged. (4) CLEAR THE SERVICE WORKER, airplane mode, hard reload - all five photographs still render offline. THIS IS THE CHECK THAT MATTERS FOR THIS SHIP: an online browser will happily fetch the new path from the network even if the precache entry were wrong, so only the offline pass proves the cache key actually matches.
